skill.name: streaming-api-patterns
skill.description: Provides implementation patterns for SSE, WebSockets, ReadableStream backpressure, reconnection, and streamed LLM responses in TypeScript applications.
skill.summary: Build and review reliable real-time streaming APIs with practical TypeScript patterns and checklists.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: Static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and TypeScript template literals; no shell execution exists. Network calls are expected examples for a streaming API skill and use local, relative, or standards documentation URLs. Two separate medium-risk example defects remain: unescaped error serialization and an unauthenticated, unvalidated WebSocket broadcast.

remediation.issue: SSE errors are interpolated into JSON text and exposed to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize a fixed public error object with JSON.stringify, log internal details server-side, and reject newline characters in SSE fields.

remediation.issue: The WebSocket broadcast example accepts and forwards every message without access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require authentication, validate origins and message schemas, enforce size and rate limits, and authorize recipients before broadcasting.

content.value_statement: Real-time APIs often fail under disconnects, slow consumers, and malformed stream handling. This skill provides focused SSE, WebSocket, ReadableStream, and LLM streaming patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose SSE, WebSockets, or ReadableStream.
Provides TypeScript examples for Next.js streaming route handlers and browser clients.
Demonstrates LLM token streaming with an SSE response format.
Shows exponential reconnect logic for EventSource clients.
Includes implementation and testing checklists for security, backpressure, and performance.
limitations: Examples are reference patterns and require adaptation to each framework and deployment platform.
The examples do not provide complete authentication, authorization, rate limiting, or production monitoring.
The SSE client parser assumes complete lines per chunk and does not preserve partial frames.
The WebSocket example omits production safeguards despite listing them in the checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Streaming Transport
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SSE, WebSockets, and ReadableStream for [feature]. Recommend one based on direction, browser support, reconnection, and expected message frequency.

prompt_templates.title: Design an SSE Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript SSE endpoint for [framework] that streams [data]. Include headers, cancellation, keepalives, structured events, and safe error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Resilient Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a resilient client for [stream URL]. Include exponential backoff, jitter, connection state, partial-frame parsing, cancellation, and observable error reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this streaming architecture for [traffic profile] and [deployment platform]. Address authentication, authorization, backpressure, proxy buffering, rate limits, load testing, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Choose a transport for one-way AI response tokens in a browser.
output: Recommendation: Server-Sent Events over a streamed HTTP response.
Reasons: One-way delivery matches the workload, browser support is broad, and reconnection behavior is predictable.
Implementation notes: Disable proxy buffering, handle cancellation, and measure time to first token.

output_examples.input: Review an SSE endpoint that exposes raw exceptions and never handles disconnects.
output: Priority finding: Replace internal exception text with a stable public error event.
Reliability finding: Stop upstream work when the request signal reports cancellation.
Verification: Test newline errors, early disconnects, slow clients, and proxy buffering.

output_examples.input: Plan a WebSocket chat service for many authenticated users.
output: Connection controls: Authenticate upgrades, validate origins, and authorize channel membership.
Message controls: Validate schemas, limit sizes, apply rate limits, and reject unexpected message types.
Operations: Add heartbeats, bounded queues, reconnect jitter, connection metrics, and load tests.

best_practices: Validate authentication, authorization, origins, message schemas, and payload sizes before opening or using a streaming connection.
Handle cancellation, timeouts, backpressure, and reconnection as core behavior rather than optional error paths.
Test partial frames, slow consumers, proxy buffering, long connections, concurrent clients, and controlled service failures.
anti_patterns: Do not broadcast unvalidated client messages or trust a connection solely because its transport succeeded.
Do not expose internal exception messages or build structured stream events through string interpolation.
Do not assume each network chunk contains a complete SSE event or valid text boundary.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SSE, WebSockets, ReadableStream, LLM response streaming, reconnection, backpressure, performance, security checks, and testing.

faq.question: When should I choose SSE?
faq.answer: Choose SSE for one-way server updates such as model tokens, notifications, progress events, or live feeds.

faq.question: When should I choose WebSockets?
faq.answer: Choose WebSockets when clients and servers both need frequent, low-latency messages, such as chat or collaborative editing.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are reference patterns that require authentication, authorization, validation, rate limits, monitoring, deployment checks, and stronger error handling.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Each supported assistant can apply the guidance while designing, implementing, or reviewing streaming code.

faq.question: Does the skill handle backpressure and reconnection?
faq.answer: It outlines backpressure checks and demonstrates EventSource reconnection with exponential delay. Production systems still need load testing and platform-specific tuning.
